articles.title: Service Changes on Rochdale Line Due to Planned Works
articles.excerpt: Planned works will affect services on the Rochdale line this weekend and continue until late August, according to TfGM.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that planned works will take place in the city centre and on the Rochdale line on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August, resulting in service changes.

Following the weekend works, further improvements will continue on the Rochdale line until Friday 28 August. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly during this period.

Additionally, due to a tram fault, there are currently minor delays on the Airport line. Essential improvement works will also take place at Prestwich Metrolink stop from Monday 18 May until Wednesday 19 August, although tram services will not be affected.

Passengers should note that the lifts at Failsworth tram stop are out of service, meaning there is no step-free access available. Those requiring assistance should contact the Metrolink contact centre for support before travelling.

articles.title: Burnley Man Banned from Keeping Animals After Dog Found Emaciated in Rochdale Home
articles.excerpt: A man has received a 15-year ban on keeping animals after an emaciated dog was discovered in a Rochdale property. Paul Lewis Dawson was sentenced at Tameside Magistrates' Court for animal welfare offences.
articles.content_html:
A man has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years after an emaciated dog was found living in unsanitary conditions at a property in Rochdale. Paul Lewis Dawson, 37, of Brownside Road in Burnley, pleaded guilty to three offences under the Animal Welfare Act 2006 at Tameside Magistrates' Court on 31 July.

The RSPCA began investigating on 6 August 2025 after receiving reports about a bullbreed dog named Kano being left unattended at a property on Alice Street in Rochdale. RSPCA inspector Beth Fazackerley and animal rescue officer Francesca Iraci attended the address, where they observed Kano through the keyhole and noted he appeared very skinny. After no one answered the door, they pushed wet dog food through the letterbox, which Kano ate.

Later that evening, the RSPCA returned with a police officer after obtaining a warrant. Upon entering the property, Kano was found to be in poor condition, having difficulty standing and displaying visible signs of distress. The dog was covered in fleas, had wounds on his body, and was suffering from severe weight loss and anaemia due to an insufficient diet. Rubbish and faeces were found throughout the property, creating an unsuitable living environment for the animal.

Dawson received a 22-week prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, and was ordered to complete 18 Rehabilitation Activity Requirement days and 80 hours of unpaid work, in addition to paying £400 in costs. The judge described the case as "the most serious case of animal cruelty I have ever dealt with." Kano has since been taken into the care of the RSPCA and has recovered.

The eclipse is expected to take place during the evening, leading to concerns that workers may feel the need to begin their shifts earlier than usual.

Employers are advised to consider the potential impact on their staff and to communicate any necessary adjustments to shift patterns in advance.

articles.title: Netwalk Event at Hollingworth Lake Draws Local Participants
articles.excerpt: A recent Netwalk event around Hollingworth Lake in Littleborough attracted a mix of new and familiar faces, fostering connections and conversations in a scenic setting.
articles.content_html:
A recent Netwalk event took place around Hollingworth Lake in Littleborough, welcoming both new and familiar participants. The event, held on a sunny Wednesday, provided an opportunity for attendees to engage in conversations and build connections.

Participants enjoyed the scenic surroundings of the lake, which is known for its natural beauty. The event concluded with refreshments at the Woodlands Cafe, located next to the RSPCA centre, where attendees could continue their discussions over coffee.

Organisers expressed gratitude to everyone who attended, highlighting the positive atmosphere and the chance to network in a relaxed environment. Such events are designed to promote local business connections and community engagement.

The Netwalk series aims to encourage outdoor activity while fostering professional relationships among local businesses and residents. Further events are expected to be organised in the future, continuing to utilise the picturesque settings of the area.
